reference_title: EM 1110-2-2107, Design of Hydraulic Steel Structures (USACE, dated 1 August 2022)

sections.title: Purpose
sections.summary: States the manual's purpose: LRFD design guidance for Hydraulic Steel Structures (HSS), including new structures, replacement, rehabilitation, and repair. Notes that manual criteria may exceed industry requirements due to USACE's unique structures and risks; criteria are minimums that may be exceeded for resiliency.
sections.body: This manual prescribes guidance for the design of Hydraulic Steel Structures (HSS) by load and resistance factor design (LRFD). This includes design of new structures, replacement, rehabilitation, and repair. Mechanical and electrical design considerations are addressed in EM 1110-2-2610. Commentary is provided in Appendix B. Due to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' (USACE) unique structures and their associated risks, criteria in this manual may exceed industry requirements. The criteria in this manual are minimum USACE requirements. These criteria may be exceeded by the designer to enhance resiliency as risk and economics dictate.
key_points: LRFD design guidance for HSS: new, replacement, rehabilitation, and repair
Mechanical/electrical design is in EM 1110-2-2610; commentary is Appendix B
Criteria are USACE minimums; may exceed industry requirements and may be exceeded further for resiliency
sections.applicability: Establishing the manual's scope and its relationship to industry (AISC) practice before applying any provision.

sections.title: Records Management (Recordkeeping) Requirements
sections.summary: References the Army Records Retention Schedule (RRS-A) / ARIMS for recordkeeping; see DA Pam 25-403 if records are not current.
sections.body: The records management requirement for all record numbers, associated forms, and reports required by this regulation are addressed in the Army Records Retention Schedule -- Army (RRS-A). Detailed information for all related record numbers is located in the Army Records Information Management System (ARIMS)/RRS-A. If any record numbers, forms, and reports are not current, addressed, and/or published correctly in ARIMS/RRS-A, see Department of the Army (DA) Pamphlet 25-403, Guide to Recordkeeping in the Army, for guidance.
key_points: Administrative recordkeeping requirement, not a design provision

sections.title: Delegated USACE Design Approval for Dam and Levee Projects
sections.summary: Covers risk assessment and approval/documentation requirements for deviations and waivers from mandatory design standards, which must include a risk assessment and be documented and concurred by the Dam/Levee Safety Oversight Group.
sections.body: Guidance in this manual supersedes all other previously published USACE guidance for the design of HSS. Justifications for deviations and waivers from mandatory design standards in this manual must include a risk assessment. All deviations and waivers must be clearly identified in the decision documents and design reports and must be deliberately called out within the review plan as a specific charge for the review. All proposed deviations and waivers from these mandatory design standards, including rationale, must be documented in a memorandum approved by the respective District and Division Dam Safety Officer or Levee Safety Officer and concurred by the Dam Safety Oversight Group (DSOG) or Levee Safety Oversight Group (LSOG), whichever is appropriate. The DSOG or LSOG will ensure the appropriate USACE Community of Practice leader(s) or their designated representatives are included in the concurrence process. Review documentation will account for all decisions and rationale for deviations and waivers, including the memorandum documenting approval and concurrence.
key_points: This manual supersedes prior USACE HSS guidance
Deviations/waivers require a risk assessment and DSOG/LSOG concurrence memorandum
Deviations/waivers must be flagged in the review plan as a specific review charge
sections.applicability: Governance process for any departure from this manual's mandatory provisions.

sections.title: Background
sections.summary: Lists the types of HSS (lock gates, Tainter gates/valves, bulkheads/stoplogs, lift gates, closure gates, wicket gates, penstocks, needle dams, crest/roller/outlet gates, lifting beams), the severe conditions they experience, and notes small/low-risk manufacturer-standard HSS are exempt.
sections.body: Types of HSS. ER 1110-2-8157 provides a definition of HSS. Typical HSS are lock gates, Tainter gates, Tainter and other types of valves, bulkheads and stoplogs, vertical lift gates, components of hydroelectric and pumping plants, closure gates for levee systems, wicket gates, penstocks, needle dams, crest gates, roller gates, outlet works gates, and lifting beams. Standard manufacturer's design of small size, low head, and low risk are exempted from these requirements. HSS may be subject to submergence, wave action, hydraulic hammer, cavitation, impact, corrosion, vibration due to defective seals, friction from seals and bearings, and severe climatic conditions.
key_points: Typical HSS: lock gates, Tainter gates, Tainter and other valves, bulkheads and stoplogs, vertical lift gates, components of hydroelectric and pumping plants, levee closure gates, wicket gates, penstocks, needle dams, crest gates, roller gates, outlet works gates, lifting beams
Small/low-head/low-risk manufacturer-standard HSS are exempt
HSS-specific severe conditions: submergence, wave, hydraulic hammer, cavitation, impact, corrosion, seal vibration/friction
sections.applicability: Scoping which structures this manual governs.

sections.title: Design Policy
sections.summary: 1.8.1: engineering responsibilities are prescribed by ER 1110-2-8157; HSS must be designed according to this manual and ANSI/AISC 360-16, and welding must follow AASHTO/AWS D1.5M/D1.5:2015 or AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2015, except as specified herein. 1.8.2: the manual gives the minimum requirements and replaces the expired ETL 1110-2-584; the Engineer must perform or oversee design, fabrication and installation; coordination with Operations Divisions, project personnel or end users is required during all design phases.
sections.body: [p. 2] 1.8.1 Hydraulic Steel Structures Design. Engineering responsibilities for the design of HSS are prescribed by ER 1110-2-8157. HSS must be designed according to this manual and American Institute of Steel Construction (AISC) Specification for Structural Steel Buildings, ANSI/AISC 360-16, except as specified herein. Welding requirements must follow American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO)/American Welding Society (AWS) D1.5M/D1.5:2015 or AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2015 (AWS) except as specified herein. 1.8.2 Discussion. This manual provides the minimum requirements necessary to provide for safety, reliability, and required performance of HSS and was written to replace the now expired Engineer Technical Letter (ETL) 1110-2-584. The Engineer, meeting the qualifications as defined by ER 1110-2-8157, must perform or oversee the performance of the design, fabrication, and installation of HSS. Coordination with Operations Divisions, project personnel, or end users is required during all design phases.
key_points: HSS must be designed according to this manual and ANSI/AISC 360-16, except as specified herein (1.8.1)
Welding requirements must follow AASHTO/AWS D1.5M/D1.5:2015 or AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2015, except as specified herein (1.8.1)
Written to replace the now expired ETL 1110-2-584 (1.8.2)
The Engineer must perform or oversee the performance of the design, fabrication, and installation of HSS (1.8.2)
sections.applicability: Baseline design-method statement: this manual plus AISC 360-16, and the welding codes.

sections.title: Requirement Criterion
sections.summary: Defines the manual's terms: 'will' or 'must' denotes a mandatory requirement; 'should' a strong preference; 'may' a criterion that is usable. Other suitably documented, verified and approved criteria may also be used in a manner consistent with the manual.
sections.body: [p. 2] The terms "will" or "must" denotes a mandatory requirement for compliance with this manual. The term "should" indicates a strong preference for a given criterion. The term "may" indicates a criterion that is usable. Other suitably documented, verified, and approved criterion may also be used so long as it is in a manner consistent with this design manual.
key_points: "will" or "must" = mandatory requirement; "should" = strong preference; "may" = a criterion that is usable
Other suitably documented, verified, and approved criterion may also be used so long as it is in a manner consistent with this design manual
sections.applicability: The manual's mandatory-language convention: read this before interpreting any 'must'/'should'/'may' elsewhere.

sections.title: Reuse of Existing Designs
sections.summary: All newly fabricated HSS must be designed according to this manual; existing designs used for new work must be modified to meet all provisions of this manual.
sections.body: [p. 2] All newly fabricated HSS must be designed according to this manual. Existing designs used for new work must be modified to meet all provisions of this manual.
key_points: All newly fabricated HSS must be designed according to this manual
Existing designs used for new work must be modified to meet all provisions of this manual
sections.applicability: Applies to both new designs and reuse of legacy drawings.

sections.title: Design Guidance
sections.summary: For non-carbon HSS, use the loads, load factors and load combinations in this manual; AISC Design Guide 27 for stainless steel structures; the current Aluminum Association Aluminum Design Manual (LRFD of building structures) for aluminum structures.
sections.body: [p. 2] For non-carbon HSS, use the loads, load factors, and load combinations in this manual. Use AISC Design Guide 27 for design of stainless steel structures. For design of aluminum structures, the current Aluminum Association Aluminum Design Manual is used. For aluminum use LRFD of building structures in the referenced manual.
key_points: For non-carbon HSS, use the loads, load factors, and load combinations in this manual
Use AISC Design Guide 27 for design of stainless steel structures
Aluminum structures: the current Aluminum Association Aluminum Design Manual, using LRFD of building structures
sections.applicability: Selecting the member-design standard for non-carbon-steel (stainless steel, aluminum) HSS.
